messages:
alex: Heads-up: seeing intermittent east-west packet loss on overlay (geneve) in the gpu-cluster during nightly batch inference. Services show spikes in retry latency and a few RDMA socket retransmits.

infra-bot: [alert] packet_loss_high: cluster=gpu-prod region=us-west2 affected_nodes=5 -> creating thread

sam: Where are we seeing drops? NIC counters or kernel drops?

alex: dmesg on node gpu-12 shows transmit stalls:
```
[ 12345.678901] NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 (mlx5_core): transmit queue 0 timed out
[ 12345.679012] rtnl: msgtype=RTM_NEWLINK
```
Also geneve interface shows rx_errors=600 in /proc/net/dev

maria: Can you paste `ip -s link show geneve0` and `ethtool -k eth0`? Might be GSO/GRO issue with tunneling + large packets.

alex: posted outputs:
```
ip -s link show geneve0:
3: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 12345678 packets 12345 errors 600 dropped 0
    TX: bytes 98765432 packets 54321 errors 12 dropped 0
```
```
ethtool -k eth0:
GSO: on
GRO: on
TSO: on
```

kai: MTU 1450 is unusual for us; geneve mtu usually 1420 for 1500 underlying. Could be path MTU mismatch. Also check `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and `ip link show` on the switch ports.

sam: Can we reproduce quickly? Suggest running `sudo tcpdump -i geneve0 -w /tmp/g.pcap` during a batch and dump the tunnel traffic. Also check mlx driver offload counters: `ethtool -S eth0 | grep -i vlan`

maria: We had a similar symptom when GSO + geneve produced oversized skbs, and the NIC dropped them silently. Workaround was disabling GSO on the worker host for affected nodes.

alex: I can roll that test. Disabling GSO/gro on candidate node now and will run overnight. Noting this coincides with big batch windows when sequence lengths spike.

infra-bot: [action] triage assigned to @sam, @maria. Links: logs and pcap saved to /tmp/geneve-1749849999/

kai: If disabling GSO fixes it, we should push a kernel config and schedule a coordinated reboot for the fleet. Also add a monitoring alert for `geneve.rx_errors > 100` per node.

sam: I'll gather NIC histograms and link with recent firmware updates. Could be a recent mlx5 FW that regressed.

alex: Thanks — will update thread after next run. TLDR: intermittent geneve rx_errors correlating with batch workload; investigating GSO/GRO & MTU path.
